title: Surveying a triangular riverside plot
stem:
From point A, two boundaries to B and C have lengths 120 m and 95 m, with included angle $48^\circ$. The third boundary BC follows a straight riverbank.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the length BC.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the area of the triangular plot.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Only AB and AC need fencing. Fencing costs 18 per metre and the entire plot needs treatment costing 0.65 per square metre. Find the total cost.

steps.text: Use the cosine rule with the included angle.
Combine $18(120+95)$ with $0.65$ times the unrounded area.
The river boundary is excluded from the fencing but not from the area.

title: A two-leg coastal navigation route
stem:
A boat travels 8 km on a bearing of $035^\circ$, then 11 km on a bearing of $125^\circ$. Bearings are measured clockwise from north. Ignore currents.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the boat’s final east and north displacements from its starting point.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the straight-line distance and bearing from the start to the final point.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the bearing for the direct return journey and the distance saved compared with retracing the route.

steps.text: Use east components $d\sin\theta$ and north components $d\cos\theta$.
Use Pythagoras and a quadrant-aware bearing calculation.
Reverse the bearing by $180^\circ$ and compare distance with 19 km.

title: Measuring a tower from two ground positions
stem:
Two points P and Q lie on level ground on the same straight line from a tower’s base B. Q is 50 m farther from B than P. The angles of elevation of the top are $44^\circ$ from P and $31^\circ$ from Q. Instrument height is negligible.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $BP=x$. Write two equations connecting the tower height $h$ with $x$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the tower height.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain how a 1.5 m instrument height at both points changes the height calculation.

steps.text: Equate the two expressions and solve for $x$.
The trigonometry gives the height above the common instrument level.
Add 1.5 m to get $81.023$ m; the inferred horizontal distances are unchanged.

diagramSvg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 640 380" role="img" aria-label="Two observation points"><rect width="640" height="380" fill="white"/><g fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.8"><text x="320.00" y="25.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" text-anchor="middle">Two observation points</text><path d="M128.6 300.0L128.6 70.0"/><path d="M366.8 300.0L128.6 70.0"/><path d="M511.4 300.0L128.6 70.0"/><path d="M128.6 300.0L511.4 300.0"/><circle cx="128.6" cy="300.0" r="3" fill="#111"/><text x="137.61" y="288.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="start">B</text><circle cx="366.8" cy="300.0" r="3" fill="#111"/><text x="375.78" y="288.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="start">P</text><circle cx="511.4" cy="300.0" r="3" fill="#111"/><text x="520.39" y="288.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="start">Q</text><circle cx="128.6" cy="70.0" r="3" fill="#111"/><text x="137.61" y="58.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="start">Top</text><text x="320.00" y="335.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle">PQ = 50 m; elevations at P and Q: 44 and 31 degrees</text></g></svg>
diagramCaption: Original mathematical diagram; use the stated data for calculations.
answerSummary: $h=x\tan44^\circ$. $h=(x+50)\tan31^\circ$. $x=82.3484$ m and $h=79.523$ m. Add 1.5 m to get $81.023$ m; the inferred horizontal distances are unchanged.

title: A cable across a rectangular hall
stem:
A hall measures 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. A cable runs directly from one floor corner to the opposite ceiling corner. Installation needs an additional 0.8 m of cable at each end.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the angle the direct segment makes with the floor.

parts.label: c

steps.text: Add both installation allowances before rounding upwards.
Buy 13 m; unused length is $0.959693$ m.

title: A running track and its outside lane
stem:
A running track consists of two straight sections each 80 m long joined by two semicircles of radius 20 m. The outer lane boundary is everywhere 1.2 m outside the inner boundary.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the inner boundary’s length.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the additional distance around the outer boundary.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the area of the strip between these boundaries.

steps.text: The two semicircles form one full circle.
The straights remain 80 m; only the semicircle radii increase.
Use the difference of two stadium areas: $2(80)(1.2)+\pi(21.2^2-20^2)$.
Using circumference difference times width alone would omit the long straight strips.

title: A straight shortcut across a circular bay
stem:
Two points A and B lie on a circular shoreline of radius 6 km. They subtend an angle of $75^\circ$ at the centre O. A path follows the shorter circular arc; a ferry travels along the straight chord AB.

title: Filling a cone-shaped hopper
stem:
A cone-shaped hopper has its vertex at the bottom, height 4 m and top radius 2 m. It contains 12 cubic metres of material, with a horizontal surface. For a filled depth $h$, similar triangles give radius $r=h/2$.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the material volume as a function of depth.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the filled depth and the vertical space remaining.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why half the hopper’s height does not correspond to half its capacity, and find the fraction of capacity at half height.

steps.text: At half height the fraction is $(1/2)^3=1/8$.
The radius also halves, so all three linear factors affect the volume.

diagramSvg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 640 380" role="img" aria-label="Conical hopper cross-section"><rect width="640" height="380" fill="white"/><g fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.8"><text x="320.00" y="25.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" text-anchor="middle">Conical hopper cross-section</text><path d="M320.0 300.0L205.0 70.0"/><path d="M205.0 70.0L435.0 70.0"/><path d="M435.0 70.0L320.0 300.0"/><circle cx="320.0" cy="300.0" r="3" fill="#111"/><text x="329.00" y="288.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="start">Vertex</text><circle cx="205.0" cy="70.0" r="3" fill="#111"/><text x="214.00" y="58.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="start">Top rim</text><circle cx="435.0" cy="70.0" r="3" fill="#111"/><text x="444.00" y="58.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="start">Top rim</text><text x="320.00" y="335.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle">Full height 4 m; full radius 2 m</text><text x="320.00" y="354.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle">Horizontal material surface; radius = half depth</text></g></svg>
diagramCaption: Original mathematical diagram; use the stated data for calculations.
answerSummary: $V=\pi h^3/12$. $h=3.5788$ m; space $0.421199$ m. At half height the fraction is $(1/2)^3=1/8$.

title: A frustum-shaped storage vessel
stem:
A vessel is a conical frustum with lower radius 2 m, upper radius 3 m and height 4 m. Use $V=\frac{\pi h}{3}(R^2+Rr+r^2)$ and curved area $A=\pi(R+r)\ell$, where $\ell$ is slant height. The vessel is open at the top.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find its volume.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find its external surface area, including its circular base.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A coating covers 12 square metres per litre. Allow 15% extra for wastage. Find the least whole litres to buy.

steps.text: Multiply the area by 1.15, divide by 12 and round upwards.

title: Locating a relay halfway through a warehouse
stem:
Two devices in a warehouse have coordinates $A=(1,2,1)$ and $B=(9,8,5)$, in metres. A relay is placed at their midpoint M. A wall socket is at $S=(5,0,0)$.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The cable must run along the floor from S to the point directly below M, then vertically up. Find the additional cable compared with a direct connection.

steps.text: Average corresponding coordinates and use the three-dimensional distance formula.
Floor length is 5 m and vertical length is 3 m.
A route constrained to surfaces is longer than the straight spatial segment.

title: A pitched roof and tile orders
stem:
A symmetrical pitched roof covers a rectangular building 12 m long and 8 m wide. The ridge is 2.4 m above the eaves and runs along the 12 m length. Ignore overhangs.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the total roof area.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Tiles cover 0.18 square metres each. Allow 8% extra and buy packs of 20. Find the least number of packs.

steps.text: Use a right triangle with horizontal run 4 m and rise 2.4 m.
There are two sloping rectangles, each 12 m long.
Use area times 1.08, divide by $0.18(20)$, then round up.

title: Dividing an irregular quadrilateral
stem:
A quadrilateral ABCD is divided by diagonal AC, which is 85 m long. The sides AB and AD are 60 m and 70 m. Angles BAC and CAD are $70^\circ$ and $55^\circ$, on opposite sides of AC.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the area of ABCD.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the two unknown boundary lengths BC and CD.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A path follows the diagonal AC. Explain why including AC when calculating the exterior perimeter is an error.

steps.text: Add the areas of triangles ABC and ACD using the included angles.
Apply the cosine rule separately in the two triangles.
AC is internal to the quadrilateral, separating two triangles.
The exterior perimeter consists only of AB, BC, CD and DA.

title: A wheelchair ramp with a landing
stem:
A ramp rises 0.72 m. Regulations allow a maximum slope of 1 vertical to 12 horizontal. A horizontal landing of length 1.5 m is required at the top. The available horizontal space is 10.0 m.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the minimum horizontal run of the sloping part and its inclination.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine whether the ramp and landing fit into the available space.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: If the landing cannot change, find the greatest rise that can be accommodated within 10.0 m.

steps.text: They do not fit; the shortfall is 0.14 m.
The sloping run can be at most $10-1.5=8.5$ m.
The existing 0.72 m rise exceeds this, so another layout is needed.

title: A service boundary between two clinics
stem:
Two clinics are at $A=(2,2)$ and $B=(10,6)$ on a rectangular district $0\leq x\leq12$, $0\leq y\leq10$, in kilometres. Patients use the nearer clinic, measured by straight-line distance.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the boundary where patients are equally far from A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine which clinic serves $P=(8,7)$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the area of B’s service region inside the district.

steps.text: The midpoint is $(6,4)$ and AB has gradient $1/2$.
The boundary meets the top at $(3,10)$ and right side at $(12,-8)$ outside the district; within the district it meets the bottom at $(8,0)$.
B’s area is the trapezium to the right: $\frac12[(12-3)+(12-8)](10)$.

title: The point shared by three emergency-service cells
stem:
Fire stations are at $A=(2,2)$, $B=(10,2)$ and $C=(6,8)$, in kilometres. The illustrated Voronoi diagram assigns each location to its nearest station.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the boundary equation between A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the Voronoi vertex shared by all three cells.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find its distance to the nearest station and explain why this distance is the same for all three stations.

steps.text: AB is horizontal and its midpoint has $x=6$.
On $x=6$, equate squared distances to A and C: $16+(y-2)^2=(y-8)^2$.
The vertex lies on pairwise perpendicular bisectors, so all three distances are equal.

title: Adding a new parcel collection point
stem:
Existing collection points are $A=(2,2)$, $B=(10,2)$ and $C=(6,8)$. A new point is proposed at $D=(6,4)$. A resident is at $P=(6,3)$. All coordinates are in kilometres.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the resident’s nearest existing collection point and distance.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: After D opens, find the resident’s nearest collection point and the reduction in distance.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the new boundary between C and D and explain which parts of existing cells can change when D is added.

steps.text: A and B are equally nearest, at $\sqrt{17}=4.12$ km.
The new C–D boundary lies on $y=6$.
Only locations closer to D than to every existing point transfer to D; all other locations keep their previous nearest existing point.

title: Nearest-station rainfall estimation
stem:
A rectangular farming district is $0\leq x\leq12$, $0\leq y\leq8$, in kilometres. Rain stations are at $A=(3,4)$ and $B=(9,4)$, recording 42 mm and 66 mm respectively. Rainfall at each point is estimated from its nearest station.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the cell boundary and estimated rainfall at $(7,1)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Estimate the district-wide mean rainfall using the cell areas.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A third station is added at $(6,4)$ and records 90 mm. Find the new cell boundaries and the revised district-wide mean.

steps.text: The equal-distance boundary is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
$x=6$; $(7,1)$ lies in B’s cell, so estimate 66 mm.
Each cell has area $6(8)=48$ square kilometres.

diagramSvg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 640 380" role="img" aria-label="Original rainfall station cells"><rect width="640" height="380" fill="white"/><g fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.8"><text x="320.00" y="24.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="17" text-anchor="middle">Original rainfall station cells</text><rect x="140.00" y="70.00" width="360.00" height="240.00"/><polygon points="140.00,310.00 320.00,310.00 320.00,70.00 140.00,70.00"/><circle cx="230.00" cy="190.00" r="4" fill="#111"/><text x="237.00" y="181.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="12" text-anchor="start">A (3,4)</text><polygon points="320.00,310.00 500.00,310.00 500.00,70.00 320.00,70.00"/><circle cx="410.00" cy="190.00" r="4" fill="#111"/><text x="417.00" y="181.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="12" text-anchor="start">B (9,4)</text><text x="320.00" y="360.00" fill="#111" stroke="none" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle">Coordinates in kilometres; straight-line distance applies.</text></g></svg>
diagramCaption: Original mathematical diagram; use the stated data for calculations.
answerSummary: $x=6$; $(7,1)$ lies in B’s cell, so estimate 66 mm. Area-weighted mean $(42+66)/2=54$ mm. Mean $[4.5(42)+3(90)+4.5(66)]/12=63$ mm.

title: Choosing between two Voronoi vertices
stem:
A hazardous-material store must be placed at one of two permitted Voronoi vertices. The sites representing settlements are $A=(0,0)$, $B=(8,0)$, $C=(4,6)$ and $D=(12,6)$, in kilometres. Candidate vertices are $V=(4,5/3)$ and $W=(8,13/3)$. Maximize the distance to the nearest settlement.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Verify that V is equally far from A, B and C.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the nearest-settlement distance at W.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Decide whether the distance criterion distinguishes the candidates, and identify one additional practical factor that could decide the location.

steps.text: Each is $169/9$, so the common distance is $13/3$ km.
Squared distances from W to B, C and D are each $169/9$.
Nearest distance is again $13/3$ km; A is farther away.
The minimum distances tie, so this criterion alone cannot distinguish them.
For example, consider prevailing winds, road access, groundwater, or flood risk; state one relevant factor.

title: How moving a site changes a service boundary
stem:
Two delivery hubs are at $A=(2,3)$ and $B=(10,3)$ in a district $0\leq x\leq12$, $0\leq y\leq8$. Hub B is moved 2 km east to $B_1=(12,3)$. Each location is served by the nearer hub.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the original and new service boundaries.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the area transferred from B’s service region to A’s.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A customer at $(6.5,7)$ says that moving B farther away increased their distance to the hub that serves them. Check this claim.

steps.text: The original midpoint of AB has $x=6$; the new midpoint of $AB_1$ has $x=7$.
The strip between boundaries is 1 km wide and 8 km high.
Originally B serves them, with distance $\sqrt{3.5^2+4^2}$; afterwards A serves them, with distance $\sqrt{4.5^2+4^2}$.
The claim is correct even though the assigned hub changes.
